findings.mitigation: Amend DECISIONS.md D-027 Track 1 sequence to verbatim match v0.2 §3: '020B → 020B.1 → 020B.2 → 020C → 020C.1 → 020J → 020K → 020D1 → 020H part 1 → 020E.a → [USER-GATE-A0] → 020H part 2 → 020D2 → [USER-GATE-A].' If it does not, DPBM enforcement is silently absent from post-pause slices that may include frontend/dashboard work (e.g., WP-SCP-023 scorecard views). findings.mitigation: One of: (a) add a sentence to DECISIONS.md D-028 rationale citing §4.6 and the subsection-verification mechanism so orchestrators reading DECISIONS.md see the rule; (b) add an explicit bullet to v0.2 §12 WP-SCP-022.1 entry: 'Plan must cite WP-SCP-022 §4.6 as the DPBM enforcement injection mechanism and include dispatch-package verification of the DPBM contract subsection'; (c) add the §4.6 requirement to ADOPT-001 §12 (020H part 3 deferred slice) as a pre-existing dispatch-contract invariant.

findings.claim: gate_check.sh --check-acc-pin returns exit 0 (WARN) — not exit 4 — when jq is unavailable or the ACC repo is not a git directory. SHA verification is silently skipped. §4.7 says 'Any drift is detected at slice-dispatch time' but does not document this degraded-path behavior.
findings.evidence: gate_check.sh lines 143–151: 'if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo GATE-CHECK WARN: jq not available — skipping ACC pin check; return 0; fi' and 'if [[ ! -d ${acc_root}/.git ]]; then echo GATE-CHECK WARN: $acc_root not a git repo — skipping ACC pin check; return 0; fi'. v0.2 §4.7 (lines 510–514): 'scripts/wp_scp_022_gate_check.sh...verifies each blob SHA against the live ACC working tree before each dispatch. Drift → pause for user review' — no mention of skip-on-missing-tooling.
findings.impact: In a fresh-clone CI environment or a context where jq is absent, the gate check passes without verifying ACC blob SHAs. A silently-unverified dispatch could proceed against ACC scripts that have drifted from the pinned SHAs, undermining the guarantee stated in §4.7. The check uses stdout (not stderr) for warnings so they may be lost in log noise.
findings.mitigation: Document in §4.7 that jq and a local ACC clone are hard prerequisites for the autonomous run, not optional. Preferably change the degraded-path return to exit 4 (same as drift) and require the user to install jq / set ACC_REPO_PATH before the chain starts. Alternatively treat WARN exit-0 as explicitly accepted and add a note to §4.7 that missing tooling is treated as a skip rather than a halt.

findings.claim: BACKLOG.md SCP-077-cost-cap row has status 'open' despite U-022-01 being closed in v0.2 §13 with the $30/slice + $300 aggregate defaults now in §8 R-022-07.
findings.evidence: BACKLOG.md line 134: 'SCP-077-cost-cap | Define review-cost cap for the autonomous chain | P1 | open | SCP-077 | Closes U-022-01 at user-gate A. Default proposal lands in §13.' v0.2 §13 (lines 730–731): 'U-022-01 (closed in v0.2): review-cost cap. Per-slice $30, aggregate $300 default per §8 R-022-07.' v0.2 §8 R-022-07: 'per-slice cap $30 (all review rounds combined); aggregate cap $300 for the full autonomous run.'
findings.impact: Low; tracking inconsistency only. Agents reviewing BACKLOG.md will flag SCP-077-cost-cap as open work requiring resolution, potentially creating unnecessary follow-up activity. The cost cap is already operative in §8/§13.
findings.mitigation: Update BACKLOG.md SCP-077-cost-cap status to 'done (in-repo)' and add to Notes: 'Default $30/slice + $300 aggregate; user may override at USER-GATE-A. Landed in WP-SCP-022 v0.2 §8 R-022-07.'

findings.claim: The D-021 reservation (2026-05-31 filing) has no BACKLOG row with a due-date anchor. §1, §10, DECISIONS.md header, and §4.7 gate helper all document the reservation, but there is no estate-visible scheduling prompt in BACKLOG.md.
findings.evidence: v0.2 §1 (line 10): 'Decisions reserved (do not assign): D-021 — reserved for the 2026-05-31 atomic workday.' DECISIONS.md lines 5–10: D-021 reservation note in document header. §5 out-of-scope (line 492): 'Operational filing of D-021 (2026-05-31 atomic workday — owned by WP-SCP-019 hygiene response, calendar-driven).' BACKLOG.md Phase 11: no D-021-filing row.
findings.impact: The 2026-05-31 filing deadline is calendar-driven and sits outside any WP's explicit deliverable list. If the session context compresses or the scheduling note in project_scheduled_followups.md memory drifts, there is no BACKLOG row to surface the deadline in estate work-tracking reviews. The §4.7 gate helper provides a collision guard post-fact but not a pre-deadline scheduling signal.
findings.mitigation: Add a BACKLOG Phase 11 row: 'SCP-077-d021-filing | File D-021 atomic-workday decision on 2026-05-31 | P0 | due 2026-05-31 | SCP-071 | Reserved per DECISIONS.md header. Calendar-driven; coordinate with Track 1 scheduler to avoid concurrent DECISIONS.md edits on that date.' Alternatively confirm that project_scheduled_followups.md memory is the intended tracking mechanism and close this nit.

r1_closure_summary.notes: All 10 R1 CRIT and 15 of 16 R1 MAJ/MIN findings are closed. m-022-05 (D-023 forward-reference) was not remedied in v0.2; DECISIONS.md D-023 rationale still points to WP-SCP-022 for expansion that never landed here.
